summary: This program is a small bakery menu app: it creates three kinds of cookie objects, prints a description of each, then prepares a gift order. It shows polymorphism at work, since one helper method handles a plain Cookie and both of its subclasses.

lines.text: Creates a plain cookie object, passing the flavor to the constructor so each object carries its own data.
A DecoratedCookie is a Cookie with extra behaviour, so it is built the same way but describes itself differently.
GiftCookie adds gift-wrapping on top of a decorated cookie, which is why it gets its own variable type here rather than being stored as a plain Cookie.
The same helper is called with three different objects; each one supplies its own version of describe().
Calls a method that only GiftCookie has, which is possible because the variable's declared type is GiftCookie and not Cookie.
The parameter type is Cookie, so any subclass can be passed in; private keeps this helper an internal detail of the class.
Java decides at run time which describe() to run based on the actual object, which is the heart of polymorphism.
